questions.question: Which internaonal observance, celebrated on 3 March 2025, had the theme 'Wildlife Conservaon Finance: Invesng in People and Planet'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Wildlife Day**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World Wildlife Day** is celebrated annually on **3 March** to raise awareness about wildlife conservation and the importance of protecting biodiversity.
 
• The theme for **World Wildlife Day 2025** is **'Wildlife Conservation Finance: Investing in People and Planet'**, focusing on sustainable finance mechanisms and the role of individuals and communities in conservation efforts.
 
• World Wildlife Day was proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in **2013**, during its 68th session, to coincide with the adoption of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (**CITES**) in **1973**.
 
• The day emphasizes the critical role of wildlife in maintaining ecological balance and the necessity of combating threats like **illegal wildlife trade**, habitat destruction, and climate change.
 
• World Wildlife Day is officially celebrated under the leadership of the **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)** and **CITES**. It aims to strengthen collaboration among nations, organizations, and communities for wildlife protection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES):**

 
 
• CITES is an international agreement between governments, established in **1973**, to ensure that international trade in specimens of wild animals and plants does not threaten their survival.
 
• CITES regulates trade in over **38,000 species**, including animals, plants, and their derivatives, through a permit system.
 
• The agreement has been signed by **184 member countries**, making it one of the most widely adopted environmental treaties globally.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife Conservation Finance:**
 
 
• Wildlife Conservation Finance refers to innovative mechanisms and funding models for financing conservation initiatives, including public-private partnerships, green bonds, and community-led projects.
 
• The focus is on mobilizing resources to preserve biodiversity, promote sustainable practices, and mitigate the impacts of climate change.
 
• Examples of such initiatives include the **Global Environment Facility (GEF)** and **UNEP's Green Finance Platform**.
 
 
 
• **Other International Observances Related to Environmental Protection:**
 
 
• **International Day for Biological Diversity:** Celebrated on **22 May**, it focuses on biodiversity conservation and sustainable development.
 
• **World Environment Day:** Observed annually on **5 June**, it is the largest global platform for environmental outreach.
 
• **Earth Day:** Celebrated on **22 April**, it emphasizes global climate action and environmental protection.
 
 
 
• **Threats to Wildlife:**
 
 
• Illegal wildlife trade, habitat destruction, pollution, climate change, and overexploitation are the primary threats to wildlife globally.
 
• Efforts to combat these threats include global treaties, national laws, and community-led conservation projects.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **World Wildlife Day 2025 Theme:**

 
 
• The theme **'Wildlife Conservation Finance: Investing in People and Planet'** highlights the importance of sustainable financial models in conservation and the active involvement of local communities.
 
• It aims to create awareness about funding biodiversity conservation and encourage global action.
 
 
 
• **Notable Wildlife Conservation Efforts:**
 
 
• **Project Tiger (India):** Launched in **1973**, it aims to conserve the tiger population and its habitats.
 
• **Amazon Rainforest Conservation:** International efforts focus on combating deforestation and preserving the world's largest tropical rainforest.
 
• **Marine Protected Areas:** Conservation initiatives to protect oceans and marine ecosystems from overfishing and pollution.

questions.question: Which Delhi Sultan captured Bukka and Harihara after the fall of the Kakatiya Kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad bin Tughlaq**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** was the Sultan of Delhi from **1325 to 1351**. He was known for his ambitious and often controversial policies.
 
• After the fall of the **Kakatiya Kingdom** (in the early 14th century), Muhammad bin Tughlaq captured **Bukka** and **Harihara**, two brothers who later went on to establish the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• The fall of the Kakatiya Kingdom was part of the broader expansion of the Delhi Sultanate under Muhammad bin Tughlaq, who sought to consolidate his control over the Deccan region.
 
• While Bukka and Harihara were captured initially, they later escaped or were released and established the **Vijayanagara Empire** in 1336, which became a significant power in South India.
 
• Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s reign is marked by his attempts to extend his empire southward, including ventures into the Deccan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**:

 
 
• He was the son of **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** and ascended the throne in 1325.
 
• Known for his ambitious projects, such as the **transfer of the capital** from Delhi to Daulatabad and the introduction of token currency.
 
• His policies often led to widespread discontent among his subjects, despite their innovative nature.
 
• He was a well-educated ruler, with interests in philosophy, science, and administration.
 
 
 
• **Kakatiya Kingdom**:
 
 
• The Kakatiya Kingdom was a prominent South Indian kingdom that ruled over the region of present-day Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Its capital was **Warangal**, which was known for its strong fortifications and cultural achievements.
 
• The kingdom fell to the forces of the Delhi Sultanate under the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
 
 
 
• **Bukka and Harihara**:
 
 
• These brothers were initially commanders under the Kakatiya rulers.
 
• After their capture by Muhammad bin Tughlaq, they managed to establish the **Vijayanagara Empire**, which became a significant cultural and political center in South India.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was known for its contributions to art, architecture, and literature.
 
 
 
• **Vijayanagara Empire**:
 
 
• Founded in **1336** by Harihara I and Bukka I.
 
• It became a major Hindu kingdom in South India, resisting the spread of Islam and protecting cultural traditions.
 
• The empire lasted until **1646**, with notable rulers like Krishnadevaraya.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Delhi Sultans:**

 
 
• **Firoz Shah Tughlaq**: Known for building canals and promoting agriculture but did not capture Bukka and Harihara.
 
• **Balban**: Focused on consolidating the Delhi Sultanate but ruled before the fall of the Kakatiya Kingdom.
 
• **Alauddin Khalji**: Expanded the Delhi Sultanate significantly, but his campaigns did not involve Bukka and Harihara.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Kakatiya Kingdom's fall:**
 
 
• The fall marked the consolidation of the Delhi Sultanate's control over South India.
 
• This event indirectly led to the establishment of the Vijayanagara Empire, which changed the political dynamics of the region.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Vijayanagara Empire:**
 
 
• Renowned for the architectural marvels like **Hampi**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The empire played a crucial role in preserving South Indian traditions and resisting foreign invasions.

questions.question: Which mountain is located in South America?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Andes Mountains** are the longest continental mountain range in the world, stretching approximately **7,000 kilometers** across the western coast of **South America**.
 
• They run through **seven South American countries**: Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, and Argentina.
 
• The Andes are known for their **high peaks**, including **Mount Aconcagua**, which is the highest peak in South America at an elevation of **6,960.8 meters (22,837 feet)** above sea level.
 
• This mountain range is also famous for its rich biodiversity and is home to a variety of flora and fauna, including the **Andean condor** and the **vicuña**.
 
• The Andes have significant geological activity, with numerous active volcanoes such as **Cotopaxi** and **Osorno**, and are a part of the Pacific Ring of Fire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rockies:**

 
 
• The **Rocky Mountains**, commonly known as the Rockies, are a major mountain range in **North America**.
 
• They stretch from **British Columbia** in Canada to New Mexico in the United States.
 
• The highest peak in the Rockies is **Mount Elbert**, located in Colorado, with an elevation of **4,401 meters (14,440 feet)**.
 
 
 
• **Alps:**
 
 
• The **Alps** are a major mountain range located in **Europe**.
 
• They extend across eight countries, including France, Switzerland, Italy, and Austria.
 
• The highest peak in the Alps is **Mont Blanc**, which stands at **4,808 meters (15,774 feet)**.
 
 
 
• **Vosges:**
 
 
• The **Vosges Mountains** are a low mountain range located in **eastern France**.
 
• They are part of the larger European mountain system and are known for their gently rounded summits, called ballons.
 
• The highest peak is **Grand Ballon**, with an elevation of **1,424 meters (4,672 feet)**.
 
 
 
• **Andes:**
 
 
• The Andes play a crucial role in the climate and geography of South America, influencing weather patterns and creating diverse ecosystems.
 
• They are home to ancient civilizations, such as the **Incas**, who built remarkable structures like **Machu Picchu**.
 
• The Andes are rich in natural resources, including **copper, silver, tin, and gold**, making them an important economic region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Andes are divided into three main sections:
 
 
• The **Northern Andes**, which are located in Venezuela, Colombia, and northern Ecuador.
 
• The **Central Andes**, which span central Ecuador, Peru, and western Bolivia.
 
• The **Southern Andes**, extending through southern Chile and Argentina.
 
 
 
• The Andes are characterized by a series of **high plateaus** and fertile valleys, making them suitable for agriculture and settlement.
 
• The Andes are also known for their **diverse climate zones**, ranging from tropical rainforests to snow-capped peaks, supporting a wide variety of ecosystems and wildlife.
 
• Some of the world's most famous trekking routes, such as the **Inca Trail**, are located in the Andes, attracting thousands of tourists each year.

questions.question: According to the Census of India 2011, which is the most Urbanised state of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **According to the Census of India 2011**, **Goa** emerged as the most urbanized state in India, with **62.17%** of its population residing in urban areas.
 
• This high level of urbanization in Goa is attributed to its status as a major **tourist destination**, strong infrastructure, and a well-developed service sector.
 
• The state has a relatively small geographical area and population, making governance and urban management more efficient compared to larger states.
 
• Goa’s economy is primarily driven by **tourism, mining, and exports**, which have necessitated the development of urban amenities and infrastructure.
 
• In contrast to Goa, other states like Kerala (47.7%), Punjab (37.5%), and Haryana (34.9%) have lower urbanization levels as per the 2011 Census.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Urbanization in India:**

 
 
• Urbanization refers to the increase in the proportion of people living in urban areas compared to rural areas.
 
• As per the **Census of India 2011**, the urban population in India stood at **31.16%**, an increase from 27.81% in 2001.
 
 
 
• **Goa’s Urban Characteristics:**
 
 
• Goa's urban development is supported by its **high literacy rate (87.4%)**, contributing to a more skilled workforce and better infrastructure planning.
 
• Its capital city, Panaji, and its commercial hub, Margao, are prominent urban centers with well-developed amenities.
 
 
 
• **Other States' Urbanization Levels:**
 
 
• **Kerala:** Though known for high human development indicators, Kerala is not as urbanized, with **47.7%** urban population.
 
• **Punjab:** With **37.5%** urbanization, Punjab’s economy is largely agrarian, with slower urban growth compared to Goa.
 
• **Haryana:** Haryana has **34.9%** urbanization, with industrial hubs like Gurgaon and Faridabad contributing to urban development.
 
 
 
• **Factors Driving Urbanization:**
 
 
• Economic opportunities, better infrastructure, and lifestyle amenities are primary drivers of urbanization.
 
• States like Goa benefit from their **small size and focused economic activities**, which facilitate faster urban growth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Census of India:** Conducted every **10 years**, the Census provides crucial data on population, urbanization, and socio-economic indicators.
 
• **Urban Growth in India:** States like Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, and Gujarat also show significant urbanization, driven by industrialization and economic development.
 
• **Urban Challenges:** Rapid urbanization often leads to issues like **overcrowding, pollution, and inadequate infrastructure**, which require sustainable planning and governance.

questions.question: Which of the following options lies between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Western Coastal Plain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Western Coastal Plain** is a narrow stretch of land situated between the **Western Ghats** and the **Arabian Sea**, extending from Gujarat to Kerala. 
 
• It comprises three distinct sections: the **Konkan Coast** (Maharashtra-Goa), the **Kannada Coast** (Karnataka), and the **Malabar Coast** (Kerala).
 
• The region is characterized by **fertile soil**, extensive coconut plantations, and prominent backwaters in areas like Kerala, contributing significantly to India's agriculture and tourism.
 
• The Western Coastal Plain is known for its **natural harbors** such as the Mumbai port, and it also serves as a hub for fishing and maritime activities.
 
• It has a tropical climate, with heavy monsoon rainfall and a diverse ecosystem, including mangrove forests and unique flora and fauna. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Malwa Plateau:**

 
 
• The **Malwa Plateau** is located in central India, primarily in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.
 
• It is known for its **black soil**, ideal for cotton cultivation.
 
• The region is bounded by the Aravalli Hills to the northwest and the Vindhya Range to the south.
 
• This plateau is famous for its historical significance, including cities like Ujjain and Mandu.
 
• It does not lie between the **Western Ghats** and the **Arabian Sea**.
 
 
 
• **Deccan Plateau:**
 
 
• The **Deccan Plateau** covers a large portion of southern India, surrounded by the Eastern and Western Ghats.
 
• It is known for its **volcanic soil** (Deccan Traps) and significant mineral resources such as iron ore and coal.
 
• The plateau is home to many rivers, including the Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri, which flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• While the **Deccan Plateau** encompasses the Western Ghats, it does not specifically lie between the **Western Ghats** and the **Arabian Sea**.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Coastal Plain:**
 
 
• The **Eastern Coastal Plain** is a broad strip of land along the eastern coast of India, situated between the Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal.
 
• It includes regions like the Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu) and the Northern Circars (Andhra Pradesh-Odisha).
 
• The area has fertile deltas formed by rivers such as the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri.
 
• It does not lie between the **Western Ghats** and the **Arabian Sea**.
 
 
 
• **Western Coastal Plain:**
 
 
• It stretches from Gujarat in the north to Kerala in the south and lies **directly between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea**.
 
• The plain is narrower compared to the Eastern Coastal Plain, with a width ranging from 50 to 100 km.
 
• It is divided into sub-regions such as the Konkan, Malabar, and Kannada coasts, each with distinct geographical and cultural features.
 
• The Western Coastal Plain is crucial for India's **agriculture, fishing, tourism**, and **trade**, owing to its fertile lands and natural harbors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Western Ghats:**

 
 
• The **Western Ghats**, also known as the Sahyadri Hills, are a UNESCO World Heritage site known for their **biodiversity** and significance as a water source for peninsular rivers.
 
• They act as a climatic barrier, causing heavy rainfall in the coastal regions during the monsoon season.
 
• These ranges form the western boundary of the Deccan Plateau and separate it from the Western Coastal Plain.
 
 
 
• **Arabian Sea:**
 
 
• The **Arabian Sea** forms India's western coastline, hosting important ports like Mumbai, Kochi, and Mangalore.
 
• It is a vital route for international trade and maritime activities.
 
• The sea is bordered by India, Pakistan, Iran, and the Arabian Peninsula.

questions.question: Which of the following shortcut keys is used to switch between open applications in Windows?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alt + Tab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Alt + Tab** shortcut key is used to switch between open applications in the **Windows operating system**. This feature is called **Task Switching**.
 
• By pressing and holding the **Alt** key and then pressing the **Tab** key, users can cycle through the thumbnails of all currently open applications to quickly choose the desired one.
 
• This functionality enhances **productivity** by allowing users to navigate between multiple programs and windows efficiently, without using a mouse.
 
• The **Alt + Tab** feature has been part of Microsoft Windows since its early versions and is widely recognized as a core keyboard shortcut for multitasking.

questions.question: The Sarkaria Commission primarily focussed on strengthening which type of federalism in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Co-operative federalism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sarkaria Commission** was established in **1983** by the Government of India to review the center-state relations and suggest reforms for enhancing cooperation between them.
 
• The commission focused on strengthening **cooperative federalism**, which emphasizes collaboration and mutual trust between the center and the states in India.
 
• It provided recommendations for maintaining a balance of power between the central and state governments, ensuring that both could work harmoniously towards national development.
 
• One of its key recommendations was the establishment of the **Inter-State Council** under **Article 263** of the Indian Constitution, aimed at promoting dialogue and resolving disputes between the center and states.
 
• The commission also emphasized the need for consultations between the center and states before enacting laws on subjects in the concurrent list. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Co-operative federalism:**

 
 
• **Cooperative federalism** refers to a system where the center and the states work collaboratively to achieve national goals while respecting the autonomy of each level of government.
 
• It promotes shared responsibility and mutual trust between the center and states, ensuring effective governance and policy implementation.
 
• Examples include coordination in implementing national schemes like **Swachh Bharat Mission**, **Digital India**, and **GST**.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal federalism:**
 
 
• Fiscal federalism relates to financial relations between units of governments in a federal system.
 
• It involves the allocation of resources and revenue-sharing between the center and states, as guided by bodies like the **Finance Commission**.
 
• Examples include the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**, which ensures a unified tax regime across the country.
 
 
 
• **Unitary federalism:**
 
 
• Unitary federalism refers to a system where the central government holds significant authority, and states have limited autonomy.
 
• India follows a quasi-federal structure, where the center has stronger powers compared to the states, especially during emergencies under **Articles 352, 356, and 360**.
 
 
 
• **Competitive federalism:**
 
 
• **Competitive federalism** promotes competition among states to attract investments and improve governance.
 
• It is a modern approach where states independently work to enhance their economic performance and attract businesses.
 
• Examples include states competing to rank higher in the **Ease of Doing Business Index** published by the Government of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Sarkaria Commission** emphasized the need for decentralization and greater autonomy for states while ensuring cooperation and unity within the federal structure.
 
• The establishment of the **Inter-State Council** has been an important step in resolving inter-state disputes and enhancing coordination between the center and states.
 
• While cooperative federalism is the ideal approach, India’s federal structure also incorporates elements of unitary federalism, especially during times of national emergencies.

__
 
• Under **Article 244(2)** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Sixth Schedule** applies to the administration of tribal areas in the **northeastern states** of **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram**.
 
• The **Sixth Schedule** provides for the formation of **Autonomous District Councils (ADCs)** to govern tribal areas, ensuring their customs, governance, and land rights are protected.
 
• Each Autonomous District Council has legislative, administrative, and judicial powers over subjects such as land management, forest resources, village administration, and more.
 
• The provision emphasizes **self-governance** for distinct tribal communities to preserve their cultural and social practices.
 
• Other states listed in the options like Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Arunachal Pradesh are not covered under the **Sixth Schedule**. *Hence, only the states listed in Option 2 are correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Introduced to protect the rights and autonomy of **tribal communities** in the northeastern region of India.
 
• Provides for the establishment of **Autonomous District Councils (ADCs)** in tribal-majority areas, allowing them to govern independently.
 
• Each ADC has legislative, judicial, and financial powers, including the ability to collect taxes and manage resources.
 
• ADCs can make laws on land use, forest management, agriculture, water resources, and inheritance, among other subjects.
 
 
 
• **States Covered Under the Sixth Schedule:**
 
 
• **Assam:** Includes tribal areas such as Karbi Anglong, Dima Hasao, and the Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR).
 
• **Meghalaya:** Includes Khasi Hills, Garo Hills, and Jaintia Hills.
 
• **Tripura:** Includes the Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council.
 
• **Mizoram:** Includes Chakma, Lai, and Mara Autonomous District Councils.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Fifth and Sixth Schedule:**
 
 
• The **Fifth Schedule** deals with the administration of **tribal areas** in states other than those in the northeast (e.g., Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha).
 
• The **Sixth Schedule** is specifically for the administration of tribal areas in the northeastern states (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram).
 
• While the Fifth Schedule provides for a **Tribes Advisory Council**, the Sixth Schedule establishes **Autonomous District Councils** with significant legislative and administrative powers.
 
 
 
• **Autonomous District Councils (ADCs):**
 
 
• Each ADC comprises members elected by the people and some nominated by the Governor.
 
• ADCs have the authority to enact laws on land, forest management, and customary laws.
 
• They also have judicial powers to establish village courts for resolving disputes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Background:**

 
 
• The Sixth Schedule was included in the Constitution based on the recommendations of the **Bordoloi Committee**, which was set up by the Constituent Assembly to address tribal issues in the northeast.
 
• The primary aim was to balance **tribal autonomy** with national unity.
 
 
 
• **Governor's Role:**
 
 
• The **Governor** of the state has special responsibilities under the Sixth Schedule, such as modifying the jurisdiction of ADCs and approving certain laws enacted by them.
 
• The Governor can also dissolve or reconstitute an ADC if necessary.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The Sixth Schedule ensures that tribal communities can preserve their **distinct identity, culture, and traditions**.
 
• It provides a mechanism for **self-governance** and development while safeguarding land and resource rights.

questions.question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights is guaranteed under Article 14 of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Protection of life and personal liberty

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Equality before the law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 14** of the Indian Constitution guarantees the Fundamental Right to **“Equality before the law”** and **“Equal protection of the laws”** within the territory of India.
 
• The phrase "Equality before the law" signifies that **every individual is equal in the eyes of the law**, irrespective of their religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. *Hence, the correct answer is Equality before the law.*
 
• The principle of **"Equal protection of the laws"** is derived from the American Constitution and ensures that individuals in similar circumstances are treated equally by the law.
 
• This article forms the foundation for the concept of the **Rule of Law** in India, which was borrowed from the British legal system.
 
• Article 14 also serves as a basis for challenging arbitrary or discriminatory actions by the government or other authorities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Equality before the Law:**

 
 
• This principle is of British origin and ensures the absence of any special privileges for any individual or group.
 
• It mandates that all individuals, regardless of their position or status, are subject to the ordinary laws of the land.
 
 
 
• **Equal Protection of the Laws:**
 
 
• This clause, inspired by the American Constitution, emphasizes that the law shall apply equally to all individuals in similar situations.
 
• It promotes the idea of substantive equality, allowing the government to make special provisions for disadvantaged groups to ensure fairness.
 
 
 
• **Exceptions to Article 14:**
 
 
• The President of India and Governors of States enjoy immunity from legal proceedings during their term of office for acts done in their official capacity.
 
• Article 361 of the Constitution provides this exception.
 
 
 
• **Important Judgments:**
 
 
• **Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978):** The Supreme Court ruled that Article 14 is not confined to equality before the law but also prohibits arbitrary actions by the state.
 
• **EP Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu (1974):** The court emphasized that equality is a dynamic concept and is antithetical to arbitrariness.
 
 
 
• **Relation to Other Articles:**
 
 
• Article 14 complements other Fundamental Rights such as **Article 15** (prohibition of discrimination) and **Article 16** (equality of opportunity in public employment).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Fundamental Rights:**

 
 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion (Option 2):** Guaranteed under Articles 25-28, this right provides freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion. *Incorrect as it is not part of Article 14.*
 
• **Prohibition of Child Labour (Option 3):** Found under Article 24, this prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in hazardous work. *Incorrect as it is not related to Article 14.*
 
• **Protection of Life and Personal Liberty (Option 4):** This is guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution, ensuring the right to life and personal liberty. *Incorrect as it is not under Article 14.*
 
 
 
• **Significance of Article 14:**
 
 
• It is a fundamental principle in the Indian Constitution, ensuring a just and equitable legal system.
 
• It prevents discrimination and arbitrary actions by the state and acts as a safeguard for citizens' rights.

questions.question: Identify the correct combination of the abbreviation, its full form and its application.

options.text: CD – Compact Disk – Used for high-speed internet access
ASCII – Automated Symbolic Code for Integrated Input – Converts images to code
ASCII – American Standard Code for Information Interchange – Encodes text in computers
LAN – Large Area Network – Used for connecting computers across continents

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ASCII – American Standard Code for Information Interchange – Encodes text in computers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange)** is a character encoding standard used in computers and electronic devices to represent text.
 
• It uses **7 bits** to encode characters, supporting **128 unique characters**, including letters, numbers, punctuation marks, and control characters.
 
• ASCII is widely used in computer systems for **encoding and exchanging text-based data**, making it a fundamental element in the communication between systems and applications.
 
• This encoding standard is crucial for text data representation in programming, file systems, and communication protocols. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• Other options provided in the question include incorrect matches for abbreviations and their applications, as explained below.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **CD – Compact Disk:**

 
 
• A Compact Disk (CD) is a digital optical disc storage format introduced in the early 1980s.
 
• It is used to store and retrieve data, including audio, video, and computer files.
 
• However, a CD is not used for high-speed internet access, as mentioned in option 1, making the statement incorrect.
 
 
 
• **ASCII – Automated Symbolic Code for Integrated Input:**
 
 
• The abbreviation ASCII does not stand for Automated Symbolic Code for Integrated Input; this is incorrect.
 
• ASCII is associated with encoding text for computers, not converting images to code as stated in option 2.
 
 
 
• **LAN – Large Area Network:**
 
 
• LAN actually stands for **Local Area Network**, a network that connects computers within a limited geographical area, such as an office or home.
 
• It is not used for connecting computers across continents as mentioned in option 4. For such purposes, **Wide Area Networks (WANs)** are used. Therefore, this statement is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of ASCII:**
 
 
• ASCII has been integral in the evolution of computer systems, allowing machines to communicate using a standardized set of characters.
 
• It laid the foundation for more advanced encoding systems like **Unicode**, which supports a much larger set of characters, including those from various languages worldwide.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **ASCII’s Key Features:**

 
 
• Uses **7 bits**, allowing representation of **128 characters**.
 
• Includes **control characters** such as newline, tab, and backspace, in addition to printable characters.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of ASCII:**
 
 
• Limited to English characters, making it insufficient for global use.
 
• Led to the development of extended ASCII (8-bit) and later Unicode (16-bit or more).
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Used in programming languages for representing characters.
 
• Serves as a foundation for text-based communication in protocols like HTTP, FTP, and SMTP.

questions.question: Where is the primary focus of the Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY)?

• The **Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY)** was launched in **September 2001** by merging two earlier schemes: the Employment Assurance Scheme (EAS) and the Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana (JGSY).
 
• The primary focus of this scheme is on **Rural areas**, aiming to provide wage employment to the rural poor and create durable community assets.
 
• The scheme emphasizes the involvement of **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)** in planning and implementing projects, ensuring local participation and development.
 
• Under SGRY, wages are paid partly in cash and partly in kind (food grains), ensuring both income and food security for rural workers.
 
• The key beneficiaries of the scheme are individuals living below the poverty line in rural areas, with a special focus on women, Scheduled Castes (SCs), and Scheduled Tribes (STs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY):**

 
 
• The scheme aims to provide **additional wage employment** in rural areas and ensure food security through the distribution of food grains.
 
• It focuses on creating **durable and productive community assets** like roads, irrigation canals, and school buildings in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Funding Mechanism:**
 
 
• The scheme is funded by the **Government of India** and the respective **state governments**.
 
• The cost-sharing ratio between the Central and State governments is **75:25**.
 
• Food grains are provided free of cost to the states by the Central government as part of the scheme.
 
 
 
• **Implementation and Monitoring:**
 
 
• The scheme is implemented through **Panchayati Raj Institutions**, which play a key role in identifying local needs and executing projects.
 
• Monitoring is conducted at the **district, state, and central levels** to ensure effective implementation and transparency.
 
 
 
• **Target Beneficiaries:**
 
 
• The scheme targets rural households, especially those living below the poverty line (BPL).
 
• Special emphasis is placed on providing employment opportunities to **women**, **Scheduled Castes (SCs)**, and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of SGRY:**

 
 
• SGRY contributes significantly to reducing rural unemployment and ensuring food security for vulnerable sections of society.
 
• The scheme also aids in rural development through the creation of durable assets, which improve infrastructure and living standards in villages.
 
 
 
• **Transition to Other Schemes:**
 
 
• In 2006, SGRY was subsumed under the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**, which provides a legal guarantee for 100 days of wage employment to rural households.
 
• MGNREGA expanded on the objectives of SGRY by incorporating a rights-based approach to employment and ensuring transparency and accountability in implementation.

__
 
• **Communal tensions** were a major factor leading to the Partition of India in **1947**. Historical animosities between Hindus and Muslims were fueled by divisive politics, leading to widespread mistrust and violence.
 
• The **Two-Nation Theory**, proposed by the All-India Muslim League under the leadership of **Mohammad Ali Jinnah**, advocated for the creation of a separate Muslim state due to the belief that Hindus and Muslims could not coexist peacefully. This was a pivotal ideological foundation for Partition.
 
• Political disagreements between the **Indian National Congress** (INC) and the **Muslim League** further deepened the divide. While the INC advocated for a united India, the Muslim League pushed for the creation of Pakistan.
 
• The rise in communal riots and violence, particularly during the **Direct Action Day** in **1946**, showcased the deep-seated tensions and made Partition seem inevitable as a solution to halt the bloodshed.
 
• The **Mountbatten Plan** of June 3, **1947**, proposed the division of British India into India and Pakistan, which was accepted by both INC and the Muslim League, thereby formalizing the Partition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Two-Nation Theory:**

 
 
• This theory was based on the idea that **Hindus and Muslims were two distinct nations** with their own customs, religion, and traditions, and therefore, they could not coexist peacefully.
 
• It was strongly advocated by **Mohammad Ali Jinnah**, the leader of the Muslim League, who argued that Muslims needed a separate homeland to ensure their cultural and religious practices.
 
 
 
• **Role of British Administration:**
 
 
• The **divide-and-rule policy** adopted by the British exacerbated communal tensions between Hindus and Muslims.
 
• By supporting the Muslim League and limiting the influence of INC, the British contributed to the political disagreements that ultimately led to Partition.
 
 
 
• **Impact of World War II:**
 
 
• The economic strain and weakening grip of Britain following **World War II** made it difficult for the colonial power to manage India effectively.
 
• As a result, the British government expedited the process of granting independence to India, leading to the rushed Partition of the country.
 
 
 
• **Partition of Bengal (1905):**
 
 
• The seeds of communal division were sown during the **Partition of Bengal** in **1905**, carried out by Lord Curzon.
 
• This division was seen as a deliberate attempt to split the Hindu and Muslim populations of Bengal, laying the groundwork for future communal tensions.
 
 
 
• **Consequences of Partition:**
 
 
• The Partition led to the creation of two independent nations, **India** and **Pakistan**, on **August 15, 1947**, and **August 14, 1947**, respectively.
 
• It resulted in one of the largest migrations in human history, with an estimated **15 million people** displaced and approximately **1-2 million deaths** due to communal violence.
 
• The political and cultural landscape of South Asia was irrevocably altered as a result of Partition.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Direct Action Day:**

 
 
• Also known as the **Great Calcutta Killings**, it occurred on **August 16, 1946**, following the call for protests by the Muslim League.
 
• The day witnessed widespread communal violence in **Calcutta**, further solidifying the demand for Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Mountbatten Plan:**
 
 
• Proposed by **Lord Louis Mountbatten**, the last Viceroy of India, it outlined the steps for the Partition of British India.
 
• The plan included provisions for dividing the country based on religious lines and allowing princely states to choose between India and Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Radcliffe Line:**
 
 
• The boundary demarcation line between India and Pakistan was drawn by **Cyril Radcliffe**.
 
• It was finalized on **August 17, 1947**, two days after the independence of India and Pakistan.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers belongs to the Peninsular Plateau?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna River**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Krishna River** is one of the major rivers of the **Peninsular Plateau** in India.
 
• The Krishna River originates from the **Western Ghats** near Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra and flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The river is approximately **1,400 km long** and is the fourth-largest river in India in terms of water flow.
 
• The river supports agriculture and is a key source of irrigation for crops like rice, sugarcane, and cotton in the region.
 
• The Krishna River basin includes major dams such as the **Srisailam Dam** and **Nagarjuna Sagar Dam**, contributing to water management and hydroelectric power generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lohit River:**

 
 
• The Lohit River is a tributary of the Brahmaputra River and flows through the northeastern region of India, mainly in **Arunachal Pradesh.**
 
• It originates from the eastern Himalayas in Tibet and is known for its swift currents.
 
• The Lohit River is not part of the Peninsular Plateau but is significant for the ecology and hydrology of the Brahmaputra basin.
 
 
 
• **Beas River:**
 
 
• The Beas River flows in the northern part of India, primarily in **Himachal Pradesh and Punjab.**
 
• It originates from the Himalayas near Rohtang Pass and is a tributary of the Indus River.
 
• Being part of the northern river system, it does not belong to the Peninsular Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Dibang River:**
 
 
• The Dibang River is another tributary of the Brahmaputra River and flows through Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• It originates from the Mishmi Hills in the Himalayas and has a steep gradient with high water velocity.
 
• Since it belongs to the northeastern region, it does not form part of the Peninsular Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Peninsular Plateau Rivers:**
 
 
• Rivers originating in the Peninsular Plateau include **Godavari**, **Krishna**, **Kaveri**, and **Narmada.**
 
• These rivers are generally seasonal, depending significantly on monsoon rainfall.
 
• Unlike the northern Himalayan rivers, these rivers do not carry perennial snowmelt water.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Peninsular Plateau:**

 
 
• The Peninsular Plateau is one of the oldest landforms in India and consists of hard igneous and metamorphic rocks.
 
• It is characterized by flat-topped hills and valleys and is divided into the Central Highlands and the Deccan Plateau.
 
• Rivers originating from this plateau flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal, except for rivers like Narmada and Tapi, which flow westward.
 
 
 
• **Rivers of India:**
 
 
• India has a diverse river system categorized into **Himalayan Rivers** and **Peninsular Rivers.**
 
• Himalayan rivers are snow-fed and perennial, while Peninsular rivers are rain-fed and seasonal.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most abundant protein in the biosphere?

• This enzyme is responsible for fixing atmospheric **carbon dioxide** into organic molecules during the Calvin cycle in plants, algae, and cyanobacteria.
 
• RuBisCO is found in the chloroplasts of plants and other photosynthetic organisms. Its abundance is due to its essential role in photosynthesis and the massive biomass of photosynthetic organisms on Earth.
 
• Given its global presence and significance in the carbon cycle, RuBisCO is integral to sustaining life on Earth by contributing to the production of oxygen and organic material.
 
• While proteins like collagen, myosin, and GLUT-4 are important in animal systems, they do not come close to RuBisCO in terms of abundance globally.

questions.question: In which of the following years did Lord Curzon pass the Indian Universities Act, imposing strict control over Indian universities?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Curzon**, who served as the **Viceroy of India** from **1899 to 1905**, is known for implementing various reforms in India, including educational reforms.
 
• The **Indian Universities Act** was passed in **1904** under Lord Curzon's administration to bring about significant changes in the functioning and structure of universities in India.
 
• The Act aimed to impose **greater control and regulation** over Indian universities, which were perceived to have become centers of nationalist activities.
 
• Key provisions of the Act included stricter state supervision, increasing the **standard of education**, and ensuring better management of universities.
 
• This Act led to widespread criticism from Indian leaders and educators, as it was seen as an attempt to curb academic freedom and nationalist sentiments in educational institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lord Curzon's Reforms:**

 
 
• Lord Curzon introduced several administrative reforms, including improvements in police, irrigation, and railways, alongside educational reforms.
 
• The **Indian Universities Act, 1904**, was intended to modernize and standardize higher education in India but was criticized for being authoritarian.
 
• He also established the **Archaeological Survey of India** to preserve India’s cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Indian Universities Act:**
 
 
• The Act increased government control over universities, including appointments, curricula, and administration.
 
• It introduced measures to raise educational standards but also restricted academic autonomy.
 
• The Act was seen as an instrument to suppress nationalist movements within educational institutions.
 
 
 
• **Educational Landscape in India (Pre-1904):**
 
 
• Universities like **Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras** were established in 1857 but had limited government oversight.
 
• These universities were criticized for focusing more on examinations than on actual learning and research.
 
• Lord Curzon aimed to address these shortcomings through the Act but faced backlash for his approach.
 
 
 
• **Reactions to the Act:**
 
 
• The Act was opposed by prominent Indian leaders, including **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**, who viewed it as an attack on academic freedom.
 
• It fueled nationalist sentiments and contributed to the growing demand for self-governance.
 
• The Act is often considered a pivotal moment in the evolution of the Indian nationalist movement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Indian Universities Act, 1904:**

 
 
• This Act brought universities under more direct control of the colonial administration.
 
• It restricted the autonomy of universities, introduced stricter regulations, and increased state oversight.
 
 
 
• **Lord Curzon's Legacy:**
 
 
• While his reforms modernized certain aspects of governance, they were also seen as imperialistic and disregarding Indian sentiments.
 
• His policies, including the partition of Bengal in **1905**, were highly controversial and sparked widespread resistance.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Education in India:**
 
 
• Post-Curzon era saw increased efforts by Indian leaders to establish institutions that catered to nationalist aspirations, such as the **Banaras Hindu University** (1916).
 
• The **Swadeshi Movement** also emphasized the importance of education in fostering self-reliance and national pride.

__
 
• Armenia signed a peace treaty with **Azerbaijan** in **March 2025**, ending decades of conflict centered around the **Nagorno-Karabakh region**.
 
• The peace treaty aimed to resolve territorial disputes and establish long-term stability in the region, which has been the focus of intense international mediation efforts.
 
• The **Nagorno-Karabakh conflict** is one of the most prolonged disputes, originating in the late 20th century, as the region was claimed by both Armenia and Azerbaijan.
 
• Previous efforts to establish peace included the **2020 ceasefire agreement**, brokered by **Russia**, which temporarily halted hostilities but failed to resolve the underlying issues.
 
• The peace treaty in 2025 marked a significant diplomatic milestone, with both nations agreeing on terms for border recognition and economic cooperation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Armenia-Azerbaijan Relations:**

 
 
• The conflict traces back to the **Soviet era**, when the Nagorno-Karabakh region, inhabited largely by ethnic Armenians, was assigned to Azerbaijan.
 
• Post-Soviet independence in the 1990s saw a war between Armenia and Azerbaijan, leading to massive displacement and thousands of casualties.
 
• Despite multiple attempts at negotiation, including efforts by the **OSCE Minsk Group**, a long-term solution remained elusive for decades.
 
 
 
• **Impact of 2020 Conflict:**
 
 
• In **September 2020**, renewed fighting erupted, resulting in significant military and civilian casualties.
 
• The **Russia-brokered ceasefire** in November 2020 resulted in Azerbaijan reclaiming territories it had lost in the earlier conflict.
 
• While the ceasefire brought temporary relief, unresolved tensions persisted, necessitating further negotiations.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Importance:**
 
 
• The Nagorno-Karabakh region is strategically significant due to its location in the **South Caucasus**, a crossroads between Europe and Asia.
 
• Regional powers like **Russia, Turkey, and Iran** have vested interests in the stability of the area, influencing diplomatic efforts.
 
• The peace treaty also opened avenues for economic cooperation, including energy transit and trade routes.
 
 
 
• **Role of International Mediation:**
 
 
• The **OSCE Minsk Group**, co-chaired by Russia, the United States, and France, has been actively involved in mediation efforts since the 1990s.
 
• International organizations like the **United Nations** and the **European Union** have also advocated for peaceful resolution and humanitarian aid for displaced populations.
 
• The 2025 treaty was seen as a culmination of years of diplomacy and pressure from global stakeholders.
 
 
 
• **Future Prospects:**
 
 
• The treaty emphasized mutual respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, setting a precedent for other conflict-ridden regions.
 
• Continued international support and monitoring are crucial to ensure the success of the agreement and prevent future hostilities.
 
• Efforts are underway to rebuild trust and foster economic partnerships between Armenia and Azerbaijan.

questions.question: What does Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) deal with?

__
 
• **Section 498A** of the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** deals with cruelty towards a married woman by her husband or his relatives.
 
• The term "cruelty" is defined under this section and includes **any conduct that causes grave physical or mental injury** to the woman or drives her to commit suicide.
 
• This section was introduced in **1983** to protect women from harassment and cruelty related to dowry demands, which were prevalent during that period.
 
• Under Section 498A, the offense is considered **cognizable, non-bailable, and non-compoundable**, emphasizing its seriousness.
 
• The punishment for cruelty under Section 498A includes **imprisonment for up to 3 years** and may also include a fine.
 
• Cases filed under Section 498A often pertain to **domestic abuse, harassment, or dowry-related issues**, making it a significant legal tool for safeguarding women’s rights in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Domestic Violence Act (2005):**

 
 
• This act provides civil remedies for women facing abuse within their homes, including physical, emotional, sexual, and economic abuse.
 
• It allows women to file complaints and seek protection orders, residence orders, or monetary relief from the perpetrator.
 
 
 
• **Dowry Prohibition Act (1961):**
 
 
• This act prohibits the giving or receiving of dowry and penalizes those involved in dowry-related offenses.
 
• Dowry deaths are addressed under Section 304B of the IPC, which deals with unnatural deaths of women within 7 years of marriage due to dowry harassment.
 
 
 
• **Role of Police and Judiciary:**
 
 
• Cases under Section 498A require thorough investigation by police before charges are framed.
 
• The judiciary plays a crucial role in ensuring justice while preventing misuse of this provision, as concerns have been raised about false accusations.
 
 
 
• **Other Sections of IPC:**
 
 
• **Section 304B:** Addresses dowry deaths and prescribes a punishment of imprisonment for not less than 7 years and extending to life imprisonment.
 
• **Section 306:** Deals with abetment to suicide, which may overlap with cases of harassment under Section 498A.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Safeguards:**

 
 
• Section 498A provides protection for women but has also faced criticism for alleged misuse in some cases.
 
• To address concerns of misuse, the Supreme Court in various rulings suggested mediation and counseling as remedies before escalating the matter legally.
 
 
 
• **Implementation Challenges:**
 
 
• Lack of awareness among women, societal pressure, and stigma often prevent victims from seeking legal recourse.
 
• Proper training for police and legal professionals is essential for effective implementation of Section 498A.
 
 
 
• **Statistics:**
 
 
• According to the **National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB)**, cruelty by husband and relatives is among the most reported crimes against women in India.
 
• Efforts to curb such crimes have been supplemented by community awareness programs and stricter enforcement of laws.

questions.question: Who administers the oath of office to the Governor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Justice of High Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governor** of a state is appointed by the **President of India**, as per Article 155 of the Constitution of India.
 
• The oath of office to the Governor is administered by the **Chief Justice of the High Court** of the respective state, as per Article 159 of the Constitution.
 
• While taking the oath, the Governor swears to preserve, protect, and defend the **Constitution and the law**, and to faithfully discharge the duties of their office.
 
• This procedure ensures the constitutional legitimacy and accountability of the Governor’s role in state administration.
 
• If the Chief Justice of the High Court is unavailable, the oath is administered by the **senior-most judge** of the High Court.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Appointment of Governor:**

 
 
• The Governor is appointed by the **President of India** under Article 155 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Governor holds office for a term of **five years**, but the tenure can be terminated earlier by the President or by resignation.
 
• The Governor’s role is primarily ceremonial, but they also play a key role in ensuring the state government functions within the framework of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Oath of Office:**
 
 
• The oath emphasizes the Governor’s commitment to upholding the **Constitution and the rule of law**.
 
• It is administered in the presence of the **Chief Justice of the High Court** to signify the constitutional importance of the office.
 
• This procedure is designed to ensure a smooth transition of power and adherence to constitutional principles.
 
 
 
• **Responsibilities of the Governor:**
 
 
• The Governor acts as the **constitutional head** of the state, with all executive actions taken in their name.
 
• They appoint the Chief Minister and other ministers, summon and prorogue the state legislature, and can dissolve the Legislative Assembly.
 
• The Governor has discretionary powers in certain situations, such as recommending President’s Rule under Article 356.
 
 
 
• **Relevant Constitutional Articles:**
 
 
• **Article 155:** Deals with the appointment of the Governor.
 
• **Article 159:** Specifies the oath or affirmation taken by the Governor.
 
• **Article 356:** Allows the Governor to recommend President’s Rule in case of constitutional failure in the state.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of High Court:**
 
 
• The Chief Justice of the High Court is the highest judicial authority in the state and plays a vital role in administering the oath to the Governor.
 
• They ensure the constitutional compliance of this ceremonial procedure.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Governor:**

 
 
• While the Governor is the constitutional head, the real power lies with the **Council of Ministers** headed by the Chief Minister.
 
• The Governor’s role is primarily to ensure constitutional governance and act as a link between the state and central governments.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Offices:**

questions.question: The number of prime numbers lying between 476 and 485, both included, is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Numbers ending in 0, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8 are generally not prime (except 2 and 5).

From 476 to 485, only 477, 479, 481, and 483 are remaining odd candidates.

Apply the rule of 3: 477 (sum = 18) and 483 (sum = 15) are divisible by 3.

Check remaining numbers up to prime 19 (since √484 = 22).

481 is divisible by 13 (13 × 37), so only 479 remains as a prime number.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Range of numbers: 476 to 485 (both included).

**Method Used:**

To check if a number N is prime, we test its divisibility by all prime numbers up to √N.

**Calculations:**

⇒ List of numbers: 476, 477, 478, 479, 480, 481, 482, 483, 484, 485.

⇒ Eliminate all even numbers (divisible by 2): 476, 478, 480, 482, 484.

⇒ Eliminate numbers ending with 5 (divisible by 5): 485.

⇒ Remaining odd numbers: 477, 479, 481, 483.

⇒ Check divisibility by 3 (sum of digits):

⇒ For 477: 4 + 7 + 7 = 18 (divisible by 3).

⇒ For 483: 4 + 8 + 3 = 15 (divisible by 3).

⇒ Remaining numbers to check: 479 and 481.

⇒ Approximate square root of 484 is 22, so check primes up to 19: 7, 11, 13, 17, 19.

⇒ For 481: 481 ÷ 13 = 37. So, 481 is not a prime number.

⇒ For 479: Not divisible by 7, 11, 13, 17, or 19. Hence, 479 is prime.

⇒ There is only 479, which is a prime number in this given range.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Number Definition

A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct positive divisors: 1 and itself.

Prime Checking Rule

To check if a number N is prime, find the approximate square root of N (√N). If N is not divisible by any prime number less than or equal to √N, then N is a prime number.

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is completely divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 3.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their highest common factor (HCF) is exactly 1.

questions.question: The product of two consecutive natural numbers is 6. The greater of the two numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The product of two consecutive natural numbers is given as 6.

We know that 2 × 3 = 6, and 2 and 3 are consecutive natural numbers.

The greater number among 2 and 3 is 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The product of two consecutive natural numbers = 6

**Method Used:**

Let the two consecutive natural numbers be x and (x + 1).

Formulate a quadratic equation based on their product and solve for x.

**Calculation:**

⇒ x × (x + 1) = 6

⇒ x² + x = 6

⇒ x² + x − 6 = 0

⇒ x² + 3x − 2x − 6 = 0

⇒ x(x + 3) − 2(x + 3) = 0

⇒ (x − 2)(x + 3) = 0

⇒ x = 2 or x = −3

⇒ Since the numbers are natural numbers, x cannot be negative. So, x = 2.

⇒ The consecutive numbers are 2 and (2 + 1) = 3.

⇒ The greater number is 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

Natural Numbers

Natural numbers are counting numbers starting from 1 to infinity (1, 2, 3, ...). They do not include zero, fractions, decimals, or negative numbers.

Consecutive Integers

Consecutive integers follow each other continuously in the sequence n, n+1, n+2, etc. For consecutive even or odd numbers, the sequence follows n, n+2, n+4.

Quadratic Equation Roots

For a standard quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is −b/a and the product of roots is c/a. The roots can be determined by splitting the middle term or using the formula x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a.

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 80 and their L.C.M. is 558. What are the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the given options to find the correct pair of numbers.

Condition 1: The sum of the two numbers must be 80.

Condition 2: Both numbers must completely divide their L.C.M. (558).

Only for 18 and 62, 558 ÷ 18 = 31 and 558 ÷ 62 = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 and 62.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of two numbers = 80

L.C.M. of the two numbers = 558

**Concept Used:**

Let the H.C.F. of the two numbers be h.

The numbers can be written as hx and hy, where x and y are co-prime.

L.C.M. of the numbers = hxy

**Calculation:**

⇒ hx + hy = 80

⇒ h(x + y) = 80

⇒ hxy = 558

⇒ The common factor h must perfectly divide both 80 and 558.

⇒ Prime factorization of 80 = 2⁴ × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 558 = 2 × 3² × 31

⇒ The Highest Common Factor (H.C.F.) of 80 and 558 is 2, so h = 2.

⇒ Substitute h = 2 in the sum equation:

⇒ 2(x + y) = 80

⇒ x + y = 40

⇒ Substitute h = 2 in the L.C.M. equation:

⇒ 2xy = 558

⇒ xy = 279

⇒ We need two numbers (x and y) whose sum is 40 and product is 279.

⇒ Using the quadratic equation t² − (x + y)t + xy = 0

⇒ t² − 40t + 279 = 0

⇒ t² − 31t − 9t + 279 = 0

⇒ t(t − 31) − 9(t − 31) = 0

⇒ (t − 9)(t − 31) = 0

⇒ So, x = 9 and y = 31

⇒ The first number = hx = 2 × 9 = 18

⇒ The second number = hy = 2 × 31 = 62

**∴ The correct answer is 18 and 62.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product of Two Numbers

For any two specific numbers, the mathematical product of the numbers themselves is always exactly equal to the product of their H.C.F. and L.C.M. (First Number × Second Number = H.C.F. × L.C.M.).

Co-prime Property

When two respective numbers are cleanly expressed as H×a and H×b (where H represents the H.C.F.), the fractional multipliers 'a' and 'b' must always be strictly co-prime to each other, indicating their highest common factor is solely 1.

Sum and Product of Roots

In any standard quadratic equation written as ax² + bx + c = 0, the total sum of the roots evaluates directly to −b/a and the cross product of the roots calculates to c/a. This core property reliably builds back the equation when only the final sum and product values are visibly known.

questions.question: The number 788973289 is divisible by which of the following?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For divisibility by 7, 11, or 13, group digits in triplets from right to left and find the alternating difference.

Groups for 788973289: 289, 973, 788.

Alternating difference = (289 + 788) − 973 = 1077 − 973 = 104.

Since 104 is perfectly divisible by 13 (13 × 8 = 104) and not by 7, the number is divisible by 13.

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = 788973289

**Method Used:**

Check standard divisibility rules to eliminate options.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Checking for 12: A number must be divisible by 3 and 4.

⇒ The last two digits (89) are not divisible by 4, so the given number is not divisible by 12.

⇒ Checking for 18: A number must be divisible by 2 and 9.

⇒ The last digit (9) is odd, so it is not divisible by 2, hence not divisible by 18.

⇒ Checking for 7: Divide the number directly by 7.

⇒ 788973289 ÷ 7 = 11271046 with a remainder of 6. ⇒ Not divisible by 7.

⇒ Checking for 13: Divide the number directly by 13.

⇒ 788973289 ÷ 13 = 60690253 with a remainder of 0.

⇒ The number is completely divisible by 13.

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 7, 11, and 13

Make groups of 3 digits starting from the rightmost digit. Find the difference between the sum of odd-placed groups and even-placed groups. If this difference is divisible by 7, 11, or 13, the original number is also perfectly divisible by that respective number.

Divisibility Rule of 12

A number is divisible by 12 if it is exactly divisible by its co-prime factors, which are 3 and 4.

Divisibility Rule of 18

A number is divisible by 18 if it is exactly divisible by its co-prime factors, which are 2 and 9.
</p

Solve for each degree of x separately directly from the expression:

x² terms: 4 × (3/4)x² − 3x² = 3x² − 3x² = 0

x terms: 4 × (−26x) − 3 × 4x = −104x − 12x = −116x

Constant terms: 4 × 17 − 3 × (−14) = 68 + 42 = 110

Combining the results, we get −116x + 110.

**∴ The correct answer is −116x + 110.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ [4 × (3/4)x² − 4 × 26x + 4 × 17] − [3 × x² + 3 × 4x − 3 × 14]

⇒ (3x² − 104x + 68) − (3x² + 12x − 42)

⇒ Open the second bracket and invert the signs.

⇒ 3x² − 104x + 68 − 3x² − 12x + 42

⇒ Group the like terms together.

⇒ (3x² − 3x²) + (−104x − 12x) + (68 + 42)

⇒ 0 − 116x + 110

⇒ −116x + 110

**∴ The correct answer is −116x + 110.**

Distributive Property

The distributive property states that a(b + c) = ab + ac. This rule is used to expand polynomial expressions by multiplying the term outside the parentheses with each term inside.

Combining Like Terms

Like terms are terms that have the same variables raised to the same power. To simplify an expression, we add or subtract the coefficients of like terms (e.g., axⁿ + bxⁿ = (a+b)xⁿ).

questions.question: 7 years ago, the age of a father was 13 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

7 years ago, Father's age = 2 × Son's age + 13.

At present, Father's age = 2 × (Son − 7) + 13 + 7 = 2 × Son + 6.

So, the father is currently 6 years older than twice the son's age.

Every passing year, the father's age increases by 1, but twice the son's age increases by 2, effectively reducing the gap by 1 year.

To close this 6-year gap and make the father exactly twice the son's age, exactly 6 years must pass.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the present age of the father be F and the son be S.

Age 7 years ago: Father = F − 7, Son = S − 7.

 
• 
 
 
 
 7 Years Ago
 Age: (F-7), (S-7)
 F-7 = 2(S-7)+13

 
 
 Present
 Age: F, S
 F = 2S + 6

 
 
 After x Years
 Age: (F+x), (S+x)
 F+x = 2(S+x)
 
 

 

 +7 yrs

 

 

 +x yrs

**Calculations:**

⇒ According to the past condition: (F − 7) = 2 × (S − 7) + 13

⇒ F − 7 = 2S − 14 + 13

⇒ F − 7 = 2S − 1

⇒ F = 2S + 6 ... (Equation 1)

Let after 'x' years, the father's age be exactly twice the son's age.

⇒ (F + x) = 2 × (S + x)

⇒ F + x = 2S + 2x

⇒ x = F − 2S

Substitute the value of (F − 2S) from Equation 1 into the above step:

⇒ x = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The age difference between two individuals always remains the same at any point in time, whether it is in the past, present, or future.

Base Variable Representation

Always assume the present age as the primary variable (e.g., x). Ages 'n' years ago become (x − n), and ages 'n' years hence become (x + n).

questions.question: What smallest number should be added to 57846 so that the sum is completely divisible by 58?

Consider the nearest easy multiple of 58, which is 58 × 1000 = 58000.

Find the difference: 58000 − 57846 = 154.

Divide the difference by 58: 154 ÷ 58 gives a remainder of 38.

Since 57846 is exactly 38 short of the next multiple (58000 − 116 = 57884), we must add 38.

**∴ The correct answer is 38.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Dividend = 57846

Divisor = 58

**Formula Used:**

Smallest number to be added = Divisor − Remainder

**Calculations:**

⇒ Divide 57846 by 58 using the standard long division method.

⇒ 57846 = (58 × 997) + 20

⇒ Here, the quotient is 997 and the remainder obtained is 20.

⇒ To make the given number exactly divisible by 58, the sum of the remainder and the new number must be equal to the divisor.

⇒ Required number to add = Divisor − Remainder

⇒ Required number = 58 − 20 = 38

**∴ The correct answer is 38.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Division Algorithm

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder. This fundamental relationship forms the basis of all divisibility rules.

Number to be Subtracted

To find the smallest number to be subtracted so that the remaining number is perfectly divisible by a divisor D, you simply subtract the Remainder directly.

Number to be Added

To find the smallest positive number to be added so that the resulting sum is completely divisible, use the formula: Smallest Additive = Divisor − Remainder.
